land.text: the Qin commanderies of Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang in Lingnan, founded 214 BC and run by Zhao Tuo; Cliopatria's shape without Âu Lạc's land

predecessors.note: Infobox: preceded by 'Qin dynasty' and 'Âu Lạc'. Âu Lạc stayed independent until Zhao Tuo annexed it in 179 BC (ledger), so only the Qin commanderies are the birth land. Cliopatria starts the row in 206, two years before the kingdom's 204.

land.text: 'divided into the seven commanderies of Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, and Rinan' (Nanyue page), with Hainan inside the page's extent

successors.note: Infobox: succeeded by 'Western Han dynasty'; the Nanyue page: 'By the year's end [111 BC], the army had destroyed Nanyue and established Han rule.'

capitals.name: Panyu (Guangzhou)
capitals.note: Nanyue page: 'Zhao Tuo founded the Kingdom of Nanyue, with Panyu as capital'; it fell to Yang Pu's men in the winter of 111 BC. Infobox capital: Panyu.

rulers.name: Zhao Tuo (King Wu)
rulers.note: Nanyue rulers table: 'Zhào Tuó ... Wǔ Wáng ... 203–137 BC'; the infobox and text begin the reign in 204 BC, the founding year used here.

rulers.name: Zhao Xing (King Ai)
rulers.note: Rulers table: 113–112 BC; killed in Lü Jia's coup of 112 BC.

rulers.name: Zhao Jiande (King Yang)
rulers.note: Rulers table: 112–111 BC; Nanyue falls to the Han in 111 BC.

keyframe_review.note: 351,993 km2 (1,286 grid cells): Guangdong 424, Guangxi 519, Vietnam 326 cells, no Hainan and no southern Fujian, which the Nanyue page lists in the kingdom's extent. Two corrections. Years: the page founds the kingdom in 204 ('In 204 BC, Zhao Tuo founded the Kingdom of Nanyue'), so the shape holds 204-203; 206-205 is Zhao Tuo holding the Qin's Nanhai without a kingdom. Land: all 493 cells of Cliopatria's Âu Lạc shape (257-179 BC in the au-lac dossier) lie inside this outline, but the page has Âu Lạc annexed only in 179 BC, so the delta is cut out until then. Hainan is added from the extent sentence, which is undated. The page gives no area.

correction.text: the shape without Âu Lạc's land, holds 202-180 BC, with Hainan added

keyframe_review.note: 351,448 km2, the same outline as 206 (4 cells differ). Same corrections: Âu Lạc's land is not Nanyue's until 179 (the shape holds 202-180 without it), Hainan is added. Zhao Tuo accepts Han's seal in 196 (vassal_start) and breaks with it in 183 (vassal_end); Minyue becomes a subject kingdom from 183 (ledger).

correction.text: the 202 shape as drawn, now including Âu Lạc's delta (annexed 179 BC), with Hainan added

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 179-171 BC: Cliopatria keeps one outline for 202-171 but Âu Lạc joins in 179 ('in 179 BC Zhao Tuo marched southward and successfully annexed Âu Lạc'; Nanyue 'divided Xiang Commandery into the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen Commanderies'). From here the 202 outline is right, with Hainan.

correction.text: the 170 shape as drawn, but only its core is direct rule: the cells of Minyue's 126 shape are vassal land (subject kingdom, 183-135 BC); Hainan added; holds to 136 BC

keyframe_review.note: 620,249 km2 (2,463 cells): the core plus the 1,177 cells of Minyue's 126 shape (Fujian 458, Jiangxi 498, eastern Guangdong 203). The page has no direct rule there: 'Zhao Tuo then annexed the neighboring state of Minyue in the east as subject kingdom', 'they were not strictly under Nanyue control', and Minyue 'submitted to Nanyue' in the second stage, 183-135 BC. So the extra cells are vassal land (a lighter tint of Nanyue's colour), not core. Cliopatria changes the shape in 170 and back in 126, but the page's stage runs 183-135: the vassal tint holds 183-136 (ledger), the 126 outline from 135 (nanyue_-135). Compared with the page's extent (Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, southern Fujian, northern Vietnam), the 170 shape is too big, not too small.

correction.text: the 126 shape as drawn (core without Minyue), with Hainan added

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 135-127 BC: 'The third stage began in 135 BC when King Wang Ying attacked a weakened Nanyue'; Minyue is no longer a subject. Cliopatria draws the 620,000 km2 outline to 127 and the 351,000 km2 one from 126, nine years late.

351,448 km2, the core without Minyue, to the fall of Panyu in the winter of 111 BC. Fits the page's extent ('Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hong Kong, Macau, southern Fujian and central to northern Vietnam') except Hainan and the southern Fujian coast, which the shape lacks; Hainan is added in nanyue_-135 (and here by reference).

region.text: the Qin commanderies of Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang round Panyu: Cliopatria's Lingnan shape without the Âu Lạc delta

ledger.note: 204: Zhao Tuo founds the Kingdom of Nanyue at Panyu. 'In 204 BC, Zhao Tuo founded the Kingdom of Nanyue, with Panyu as capital, and declared himself the Martial King of Nanyue'; in 214 'the Qin court established the Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang Commanderies' and he 'was made magistrate of Longchuan'. The Zhao Tuo page: infobox reign 203-137, body 'in 204 BC'. Year from the page; the land is Cliopatria's Lingnan shape minus Âu Lạc (reading).

region.text: the kingdom of Nanyue, a nominal Han vassal

ledger.note: 196: Zhao Tuo submits to the Han. 'The first period of Nanyue's subordination to the Han dynasty began in 196 BC'; Lu Jia was sent to obtain his allegiance, 'Zhao Tuo then decided to receive Emperor Gaozu's seal and submit to Han authority', 'a vassal state while in practice it was autonomous'. The Zhao Tuo page: Lu Jia sent 'in June or July 196 BC' to 'recognize Zhao Tuo as king'.

183: Zhao Tuo breaks with the Han. 'Nanyue's first period of antagonism with the Han dynasty lasted from 183 BC to 179 BC, when trade was suspended'; he 'declared himself the emperor of Nanyue'. The Zhao Tuo page dates the embargo, the imperial title and the Changsha attack all to 185 BC; the Nanyue page's 183-179 is used.

region.text: the Minyue lands of Fujian and Jiangxi, a subject kingdom of Nanyue

ledger.note: 183: Minyue becomes Nanyue's subject kingdom. 'Zhao Tuo then annexed the neighboring state of Minyue in the east as subject kingdom'; the page's second stage of Nanyue-Minyue relations runs 183-135 BC and Minyue 'submitted to Nanyue after seeing it defeat the Han dynasty's first attack'; also 'they were not strictly under Nanyue control'. The Zhao Tuo page has Zhao menacing Minyue, Western Ou and Luo about 181 and bringing them under control after 180. Year is the page's stage; the land is the minyue dossier's 126 shape.

region.text: Yelang, 'comprising most of modern Guizhou and Yunnan Provinces' (Nanyue page); the discs are the yelang dossier's stand-in for its core in western Guizhou

ledger.note: 183: the Yi tribes of Yelang declare allegiance. 'The kingdom of Yelang and Tongshi also submitted to Nanyue rule' and 'nearly all of the Yi tribes declared allegiance to Nanyue', after Nanyue first repelled the Han (183-179) and until 'Nanyue's demise in 111 BC'. Another section says 'After 179 BC' Zhao persuaded Minyue, Yelang, Tongshi and others to submit, 'but they were not strictly under Nanyue control'. A loose allegiance, drawn as the faintest tint.

region.text: the frontier between Nanyue and the Han kingdom of Changsha, where Zhao Tuo took 'a few border towns' (Zhao Tuo page)

ledger.note: 183: the first Han-Nanyue antagonism. Zhao Tuo 'attacked the principality of Changsha' (Han's vassal kingdom of Hunan) and defeated 'the Han dynasty's first attack on Nanyue'. The page gives no year for the Changsha attack or the Han counter-attack, only the period 183-179; the Zhao Tuo page has the attack in 185 and 'taking a few border towns'. Zone: the Nanyue-Changsha frontier.

region.text: the frontier between Nanyue and the Han kingdom of Changsha

ledger.note: 179: the antagonism ends. 'Nanyue's second period of submission to the Han dynasty lasted from 179 BC to 112 BC'; Lu Jia returned to Panyu with a letter from the new emperor and 'Zhao Tuo decided to submit to the Han once again, withdrawing his title of emperor and reverting to king'. The Zhao Tuo page puts the rescinding in late 180 BC. No page names a frontier change.

region.text: the kingdom of Nanyue, a Han vassal again until 112

ledger.note: 179: Nanyue submits to the Han again. 'Zhao Tuo decided to submit to the Han once again, withdrawing his title of emperor and reverting to king'; 'Nanyue's second period of submission to the Han dynasty lasted from 179 BC to 112 BC'.

region.text: Âu Lạc: the Red River delta and the Âu Việt hills ('parts of modern-day Guangxi and northern Vietnam')

ledger.note: 179: Zhao Tuo annexes Âu Lạc. 'In 179 BC Zhao Tuo marched southward and successfully annexed Âu Lạc' and 'divided Xiang Commandery into the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen Commanderies'. The Zhao Tuo page is silent on the year (it has Zhao menacing Minyue, Western Ou and Luo from about 181). The au-lac dossier has the matching dissolve in 179.

region.text: the Minyue lands of Fujian and Jiangxi, a subject kingdom of Nanyue

ledger.note: 135: Minyue attacks and is no longer a subject. 'In 135 BC, the king of neighboring Minyue launched an attack on the towns along the two kingdoms' borders'; 'The third stage began in 135 BC when King Wang Ying attacked a weakened Nanyue'.

region.text: the Minyue-Nanyue frontier towns attacked in 135 BC

ledger.note: 135: Minyue invades Nanyue. 'In 135 BC, the king of neighboring Minyue launched an attack on the towns along the two kingdoms' borders.' Zhao Mo appealed to the Han, which 'sent Wang Hui, an official governing ethnic minorities, and agricultural official Han Anguo' with the army ordered to attack Minyue from two directions.

135: the invasion ends. The page does not say how: it has the Han army ordered to attack Minyue from two directions and Zhao Mo sending his son Zhao Yingqi to the Han capital. The minyue dossier (ea-01, from the Minyue page) has the Minyue king murdered by his brother and a peace in 135, with no land changing hands.

112: Lü Jia's coup ends Nanyue's submission. 'In 112 BC, the men crossed into Nanyue territory, and Lü Jia finally executed his plan', 'killing Zhao Xing, Queen Dowager Jiu, and all the Han emissaries in the capital'. The page's second period of submission runs 179-112 BC.

111: Emperor Wu's army attacks. 'In autumn of 111 BC, Emperor Wu sent an army of 100,000 men'; 'Yang's men led the advance into Panyu where Lü Jia and Zhao Jiande had fortified inside the inner walls'.

region.text: Nanyue, conquered by the end of 111 BC

ledger.note: 111: Panyu falls in the winter. 'By the year's end, the army had destroyed Nanyue and established Han rule'; Lü Jia and Zhao Jiande 'fled the city by boat'. The page names no month.

region.text: Yelang, 'comprising most of modern Guizhou and Yunnan Provinces' (Nanyue page); the discs are the yelang dossier's stand-in for its core in western Guizhou

ledger.note: 111: Yelang's allegiance to Nanyue ends with Nanyue ('until Nanyue's demise in 111 BC'). The yelang dossier has Han absorbing Yelang in 111.

region.text: all of Nanyue, in the seven commanderies

ledger.note: 111: Nanyue becomes Han land. 'Afterwards, the other commanderies and counties of Nanyue surrendered to the Han dynasty, ending Nanyue's 93-year existence'; its territory 'was divided into the seven commanderies of Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, and Rinan.' Hainan is in the page's extent and goes with it.
111: the Kingdom of Nanyue ends after 93 years ('ending Nanyue's 93-year existence'); the last king Zhao Jiande fled Panyu by boat.

wars.name: First Han-Nanyue antagonism (the Changsha war)
wars.outcome: Nanyue, embargoed by Empress Lü's officials, declared its king emperor, attacked Changsha and defeated the Han's first attack; in 179 Zhao Tuo withdrew the imperial title and returned to nominal submission.
wars.note: The Zhao Tuo page dates the embargo, the imperial title and the Changsha attack to 185 BC and the retreat to late 180; the Nanyue page's period 183-179 is used. Changsha has no Cliopatria row or dossier.

wars.name: Minyue's invasion of Nanyue
wars.outcome: Minyue attacked the border towns; Zhao Mo appealed to the Han, which sent Wang Hui and Han Anguo to attack Minyue from two directions. The page does not say how the fighting ended.
wars.note: The minyue dossier carries the matching contest_start and contest_end.

wars.name: Han conquest of Nanyue

zones.text: Nanyue from the coup of 112 to the fall of Panyu in the winter of 111 BC

wars.outcome: Lü Jia killed the pro-Han king and the Han emissaries in 112; Emperor Wu sent 100,000 men in autumn 111; Panyu fell that winter, Zhao Jiande and Lü Jia fled by boat, and Nanyue became seven Han commanderies.
wars.note: The page names no battle date more exact than 'autumn' and 'winter' of 111.

certainty.note: Nanyue's lands are given as modern provinces and commanderies, never as a surveyed line; the Minyue and Yelang parts are subject or loosely allied lands whose frontier is softer still.

sources.title: Nanyue
sources.note: Founding 204 BC, Qin commanderies 214, Han relations 196/183/179/112, Au Lac 179, Minyue 135, Han conquest 111, seven commanderies, extent (Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, southern Fujian, northern Vietnam).

sources.title: Zhao Tuo
sources.note: Infobox reign 203-137 BC (body: 204); emperor, Changsha attack and embargo all dated 185 BC on this page (the Nanyue page has 183-179); Lu Jia June or July 196; Zhao rescinds the imperial claim late 180. No ruler list.

notes: Cliopatria's four Nanyue shapes are kept with corrections. (1) Years: the page founds the kingdom in 204 (Cliopatria 206) and ends it in 111, as Cliopatria does. (2) Âu Lạc: Cliopatria's Nanyue outline contains all 493 cells of its Âu Lạc shape from 206, but Âu Lạc was independent until 179 (Nanyue page; the au-lac dossier has the same date); the correction cuts it out until 179. (3) Minyue: the 170-127 shape is core plus Minyue's lands; the page makes Minyue a subject kingdom (183-135), so those cells are vassal land, and the shape reverts in 135, not 126. The minyue dossier (ea-01) has its own minyue_-170 keyframe for the same cells. (4) Hainan is in the page's extent but not in any Cliopatria shape; added. Southern Fujian is also in the extent sentence but is Minyue country in the minyue dossier; not added. DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES: the Nanyue page puts the embargo, the imperial title and the 183-179 antagonism where the Zhao Tuo page has 185 for all three and the retreat in late 180; the Nanyue page is used. The Zhao Tuo infobox gives the reign 203-137 against 204 in both bodies. Nanyue is 'infobox: Establishment 204 BC'; no area on either page. Pages opened: Nanyue, Zhao Tuo (2 against a budget of up to 5; the Minyue, Au Lac and Dong'ou sides are the ea-01 and Vietnam dossiers' pages). The 'seven commanderies' (not nine) is the page's list; the Hainan commanderies of 110 BC (Zhuya, Dan'er) are not on the page. Rulers: added by reviewer ea-02-c (2026-10-19) from the rulers table of the Nanyue page (203–137, 137–122, 122–113, 113–112, 112–111 BC); the author had read the page as having no list. NEEDED FROM OTHERS: the han-dynasty dossier (this group) carries the matching gain of Nanyue in 111; yelang (vassal tie to Nanyue 183-111) has no matching vassal events in its own ledger; 'Changsha Kingdom' (Han vassal kingdom, Hunan) has no dossier.
